newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU stocks rise by 13.51 mln barrels in December.
newsitem.headline: EU stocks rise by 13.51 mln barrels in December.

text.p: Oil stocks in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose by 13.51 million barrels in December because of a rise in the levels of crude and gasoline, Stitching Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.

Crude and product stocks were up 13.51 million barrels, or 1.3 percent, in December to 1.036 billion barrels. But this left them 1.18 million barrels, or 0.1 percent lower than at the end of December 1995.
The overall monthly stock rise was the result of increases in the levels of crude and gasoline. Middle distillate and fuel oil stocks were virtually unchanged.
Crude oil stocks rose by 7.23 million barrels, or 1.8 percent, to 411.72 million barrels, almost identical to year-ago levels.
Gasoline inventories were up by 4.50 million barrels, or 3.0 percent, to 155.59 million barrels. This left them down 5.89 million barrels, or 3.6 percent, year-on-year.
Middle distillate stocks were down a modest 370,000 barrels, 0.1 percent, to 297.38 million barrels, leaving them 5.03 million barrels, or 1.7 percent higher year-on-year.
Fuel oil inventories were up 390,000 barrels, 0.3 percent, to 142.16 million barrels. They were 1.69 million barrels, or 1.2 percent lower year-on-year.
Naphtha stocks were up 1.76 million barrels to 29.04 million barrels.
Crude intake was 360,000 barrels per day (bpd) lower than in November at 11.446 million bpd, leading to a utilisation rate of 90.84 percent in October.
A full list inventory levels, including country-by-country in barrels and tonnes, will be available on Reuters pages EUROILA to EUROILJ.
